prompt.context: Your client is the CFO of Aperture Laboratories, a leading US biopharmaceutical company with a market cap greater than $150B. Aperture develops and manufactures a diversified range of products and in particular prides itself on saving millions of human lives every year. The company is under investor pressure because of its slow firm value growth over the next 10 years. Investors are very anxious to see significant changes announced at the firm in the next quarter. The CFO has already identified and evaluated a number of high-growth, promising, but capital-intensive projects, and she does not have enough cash to invest in any of the opportunities.
prompt.question: What does the CFO need to do next?

clarifying_info.q: Are there tax implications from selling any business unit?
clarifying_info.a: The deal has been structured by JP Morgan to be tax-free.

clarifying_info.q: Does the NPV figure for each project include the capital investment required?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the NPV includes the capital investment.

exhibits.title: Aperture Business Segments
exhibits.shows: A scatter chart plotting Aperture's eight business segments by Sales ($B) on the x-axis and 5-year CAGR on the y-axis, with an arrow indicating increasing specialization requirements.

exhibits.title: Investment Opportunities
exhibits.shows: A scatter chart plotting six capital projects by Capital Investment Required ($B) on the x-axis and Project NPV ($B) on the y-axis.

projects.name: Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants
Research new formulations for existing product portfolio

framework: Raise capital: identify options (issue equity, raise debt, divest a business unit, cancel existing projects to free budget)
Evaluate each capital-raising option on speed, cost, investor optics, and strategic fit
Guide toward divestiture as the preferred option given investor demand for significant structural change
Quantify proceeds from divestiture to establish a capital budget
Select optimal portfolio of new projects subject to the capital constraint, maximizing total NPV
Address remaining capital and outline a recommendation with key risks and mitigations

questions.prompt: Which business unit should Aperture divest, and why?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies Animal Health as the best divestiture candidate because: (1) it has the lowest or near-lowest 5-yr CAGR (~0%), (2) it is strategically misaligned with Aperture's human-health mission, and (3) its low specialization requirements mean a larger pool of potential buyers. Candidate should discuss pros/cons of each capital-raising method before zeroing in on divestiture.

questions.prompt: How much capital will Aperture raise from selling the Animal Health division?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the 3.5x EV/Sales multiple to Animal Health's $4.2B in sales. Result is $14.7B in proceeds. Deal is structured to be tax-free.

math.setup: Enterprise Value = EV/Sales multiple x Animal Health sales = 3.5 x $4.2B

questions.prompt: Given the $14.7B capital budget, which projects should Aperture invest in to maximize total NPV?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates calculate a profitability index (NPV / Capital Investment) for each project, rank by index, and select projects until the capital constraint is reached. The optimal selection is: (1) Research new formulations ($3B capital, NPV $5B, PI 1.67), (2) Build R&D center in China ($6B capital, NPV $10B, PI 1.67), (3) Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing ($4B capital, NPV $7B, PI 1.40). Total capital used = $13B, total NPV = $22B. Remaining $700M should be returned to shareholders (buyback or dividend). An excellent candidate will also note qualitative factors such as project timelines and execution risk.

math.setup: Profitability Index (PI) = NPV / Capital Investment for each project; rank descending; select greedily within $14.7B budget
steps: Build R&D center in China: PI = $10B / $6B = 1.67
Rank by PI: Research new formulations (1.67), Build R&D China (1.67), Cost-cutting US mfg (1.40), Acquire GLP-1 (1.11), Sales force rationalization (1.00), License respiratory (1.00)
Select top projects within $14.7B: Research new formulations ($3B) + Build R&D China ($6B) + Cost-cutting US mfg ($4B) = $13B capital, $22B total NPV
math.answer: Invest in Research new formulations, Build R&D center in China, and Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants. Total capital deployed: $13B. Total NPV: $22B. Remaining $700M available for shareholder returns.

recommendation: Divest the Animal Health division at a 3.5x EV/Sales multiple, raising $14.7B in tax-free proceeds

Invest $13B of those proceeds across three projects — Research new formulations for the existing portfolio ($3B, NPV $5B), Build an R&D center in China ($6B, NPV $10B), and a Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants ($4B, NPV $7B) — for a combined NPV of $22B
Return the remaining ~$700M to shareholders via a buyback or special dividend
risks: Inability to find a buyer for the Animal Health division or receiving a lower-than-expected multiple
Prolonged deal timeline delaying capital availability and investor-visible change
New capital projects underperform or fail to deliver projected NPV
Loss of Animal Health capabilities that may have synergies with other segments
next_steps: Formally engage JP Morgan to run a sale process for Animal Health
Secure board and management buy-in for the divestiture and the three selected projects
Develop detailed project plans and timelines for the three investments
Prepare investor communications to announce the strategic portfolio repositioning next quarter
